title: Every one-dimensional minimal prime of the completion of a Noetherian local ring is the radical of the extension of a minimal prime of the henselization
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) with henselization A^h and a minimal prime q of the completion A-hat with dim(A-hat/q) = 1, and asserts the existence of a minimal prime q^h of A^h with q = sqrt(q^h A-hat) (source lines 32099-32106). The proof is a two-stage descent. Since A and A^h have the same completion, one may assume A is henselian; then one applies the quotient-by-idempotent lemma to the surjection A-hat -> A-hat/J with J = Ker(A-hat -> (A-hat)_q), which requires proving that a power of m annihilates J/J^2: the proof obtains q^n contained in J because dim((A-hat)_q) = 0, chooses a power of m annihilating J/J^2 using that (J/J^2)_q = 0 and that m is the only associated prime of J/J^2, and concludes that A-hat/J is the completion of a finite type A-algebra C (proof lines 32109-32121). The second stage identifies C: since C/mC = A/m, the ideal m_C = mC is maximal and A -> C is unramified there; after a principal localization C is a quotient of an etale A-algebra B by the structure proposition for unramified maps, and because the residue field extension of A -> C_{m_C} is trivial and A is henselian one gets B = A after a localization, so C = A/I for some ideal I (proof lines 32124-32134). Finally the proof shows J = IA-hat by exactness of completion in this situation and I = J cap A by flatness of A -> A-hat, so with q^n contained in J contained in q one gets p = q cap A satisfying p^n contained in I contained in p, and hence sqrt(p A-hat) = q (proof lines 32134-32141). The non-routine content is the two-step annihilation of J/J^2 that makes the quotient lemma applicable, and the henselian rigidity that forces the unramified algebra to be A itself.
